session.title: Kota Kinabalu island-hopping recovery day
session.purpose: Join the confirmed three-island family outing while respecting red physical readiness and impaired CNS status from 4.93 hours of primary sleep. Preserve recovery for the return flight and the post-travel Enduro reacquisition block.

dose.family_activity: Boat transfers, island walking, shade breaks and casual water activity only.
dose.water_activity_ceiling: Easy recreational swimming or snorkeling only with a buddy or guide; no solo open-water swimming, breath-hold work, hard finning, racing, distance target or deep-water novelty.
dose.day_rule: Do not add a run, gym session, bike session, step target or intensity-minute target.

session.adaptation_hypothesis: Treating the outing as low-demand life activity should allow short-sleep CNS fatigue to recover while normal movement, daylight and family enjoyment preserve rhythm without adding meaningful training density.
execution_rules: Use a properly fitted personal flotation device during boat travel and whenever directed by the operator.
Stay with the group, buddy or guide in the water. Today is not a day to test distance, breath hold, current tolerance or technical confidence.
Choose shade and seated boat recovery whenever possible; use a hat, protective clothing and sunscreen according to the product directions.
Eat breakfast and lunch rather than using low appetite, seasickness or travel logistics as an accidental fast.
Follow the boat operator's current marine-weather decision; local conditions override the itinerary.
Finish the day feeling no more depleted than at departure.

expected_result.during: Normal family participation without exertional swimming, heat strain, delayed reactions or progressive sleepiness.
expected_result.after: Stable cognition, no disproportionate fatigue and enough appetite for a normal Cantonese dinner.
expected_result.next_day: Travel-ready at noon with no need for make-up training before or after the flight.

stop_rules: Any brain fog, unusual sleepiness, delayed reaction, dizziness, headache, nausea, poor coordination or unsafe confidence removes swimming and snorkeling; remain on shore or boat and tell the family or guide.

Heat symptoms, chest symptoms, breathing difficulty, worsening seasickness or inability to maintain normal conversation ends optional activity and shifts to cooling, fluids and appropriate medical assessment.
Thunder, lightning, unsafe sea state, poor visibility or boat-operator concern overrides all planned water activity.
Do not enter the water alone or continue because Garmin, Body Battery or the itinerary appears favourable.

nutrition.before_departure: Eat a normal breakfast with carbohydrate, protein and salt, plus approximately 400-600 ml fluid before 10:00.
nutrition.during: Use meals and snacks normally. Across the hot six-hour window, target roughly 400-650 ml fluid per hour on average, adjusted for shade, sweat and access, with approximately 300-600 mg sodium per hour during sustained heat exposure.
nutrition.dinner: Steamed fish is an excellent protein anchor. Add rice, noodles or dim sum carbohydrate, vegetables and fluids; salt from Cantonese food can support replacement but does not substitute for water.
nutrition.alcohol: Avoid alcohol tonight because sleep restoration and tomorrow's flight are the priority.
